SddInterface.keywords: interface, schema, versioning, compatibility, consumer, decision-log, sdd-interface
SddInterface.Mission:
Author or evolve an `interface` scope spec — cross-scope interfaces: schema (OpenAPI / gRPC proto / JSON Schema / GraphQL), versioning policy, compatibility matrix, consumer declaration. A self-contained living spec. Loaded lazily by the router; inherits the router core (language, dialogue, safeguard, diverge, no-narration, stateless) — not repeated here.
Input — scope name + intent (or an existing spec for refine / pivot). Output — `specs//.spec.md` (scope-type interface).
Out of scope: implementation, module decomposition, product / library design. The project portal is the root branch.
**Glossary.** Modes: greenfield · refine · pivot · rewrite. Consumers = the scopes that depend on this interface scope.

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT, AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH
BeliefState.Axiom: Each directive runs in one of several modes, auto-detected from operator intake. Mode controls step branching and which axioms apply. The concrete mode set is directive-specific (e.g. `greenfield` / `refine` / `pivot`; `initial` / `extend-dag`; `initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`).

Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.

The `scope` flow reads `specs/README.md` for project context (vision, scope graph, sibling scopes). It MUST NOT rewrite the file. The narrow exception (per the `root` flow's `AX_PORTAL_PRIMARY_OWNER`): when the `scope` flow creates a brand-new scope, it MAY append one placeholder row to the Scopes table tagged `🚧 (awaiting root sync)`. Any other edit is forbidden — run the `root` flow instead.

The scope spec is a living document. In `refine` mode any section may be updated in place. There is no frozen 7 Handoff — the Handoff section evolves as modules are added.
`pivot` uses Decision Log supersession: the old entry → `status: superseded`, body preserved; the new entry carries `Supersedes: D-NNN` and `Was → Now`. The spec body is rewritten in place; git history is the full predecessor.

A spec lives in two states. **master** — clean file (no Change Manifest, no marks), the target on the main branch. **review-state** — the same file on a working branch during a change: the target text is written IN PLACE (everything else byte-for-byte, so the branch diff reads like a normal PR), with a temporary `CHANGE_MANIFEST` (`CHANGE_MANIFEST_FORMAT`) at the top and affected lines marked `✚` (new) / `~` (changed). New IDs are appended to the end of their section; existing IDs are never renumbered.
`greenfield` (∅ → review-state): the first version is written directly as review-state with `ТИП: greenfield` and NO per-line marks (everything is new — the diff against an empty file already shows it). `refine` / `pivot` edit an existing master in place WITH marks.
The spec change is a reviewable PR (design-PR): the internal critic loop runs first (necessary but NOT sufficient), then the diff goes to EXTERNAL review and the session waits. **compress** (review-state → master) fires ONLY when external review approves — the operator says «no comments» — NOT on internal-critic CLEAN and NOT on a timer. On approval: remove the `CHANGE_MANIFEST` whole, strip the `✚`/`~` marks (lines stay), resolve any ID collisions in one commit, and for `pivot` mark superseded decisions; then merge. Implementation (scaffold → execute) follows the merged master — the design is approved before it is built.
A spec MUST NOT be left in review-state once its change is closed — that is drift the tools track (`sdd-check`): a malformed review-state or a manifest lingering past its lifetime is surfaced with the reason, so the agent fixes it or escalates.

Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.

For scope-type=interface: - Interface Declaration: schema format (OpenAPI / gRPC proto / JSON Schema / GraphQL), versioning scheme (semver / date-based / none), namespacing. - Compatibility Matrix: backward-compat guarantees, breaking-change protocol. - Consumer declaration: which scopes consume this interface scope.

Every non-trivial decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` (D-NNN, Status, Recorded, Why in the operator's wording, Risk accepted, Rejected alternatives; IDs are stable). Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.

In `pivot` mode every replaced decision: the old D-NNN → `status: superseded`. The new D-NNN carries `Was → Now` + `Supersedes: D-NNN` + a git ref pointing to the pre-rework state. Pivot Invalidation List enumerates downstream artifacts requiring `refine-module` / reopen — consumed by `audit` via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`.
`rewrite` mode is the exception: a pre-production / v0 scope with no production backing, whose old content was scratch that helps nothing going forward. It replaces the spec from a clean slate — NO supersession trail, NO Pivot Invalidation List (nothing downstream to keep coherent; git history is the only record). Use `pivot` (keep the trail) whenever the scope has any production backing or downstream consumers; use `rewrite` only for genuine v0 throwaway. Enforcement: a scope that already has downstream artifacts on disk (module specs or task tickets) is by definition NOT v0 — `rewrite` is forbidden there; halt and use `pivot`.

Scope spec declares `depends-on` edges in Scope Dependencies. These edges feed cascade computation in the `scaffold` flow. Cross-scope contracts are sourced from `interface`-type scopes — never described inside a product scope spec.

Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses in every intake-style frame. - **Facts** — directly observable from input artifacts (spec, sibling specs, rule files, extracted measurements). - **Assumptions** — working assumptions awaiting confirmation; mark explicitly. - **Hypotheses** — conjectures that require operator validation before they are promoted to requirements.
Conflating the three causes downstream decisions to be made on unvalidated assumptions, producing requirements mismatches that surface only at integration; surface them in distinct lists.

Discovery is design-blind to repository code (per `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE`) **except** inside STEP_7 (External Dependencies Audit), where narrow Read is permitted **only for inventory verification** — confirming whether a referenced package, file, scope, or tool physically exists. Permitted reads in STEP_7: `package.json` and equivalents, `tsconfig.json` and equivalents, `specs/README.md`, sibling scope manifests, filesystem existence checks. Forbidden in STEP_7: reading application source code to influence design decisions; revisiting Vision / Requirements / Architecture / Contracts based on what was found. If a finding genuinely invalidates a design decision, pop back to the relevant STEP_3–STEP_6 explicitly and treat as `pivot`.

Every interface spec carries at least one diagram in an `Overview` section, high up — who produces vs consumes the contract, or the version-transition flow, at a glance. The floor is one (mermaid or ASCII), held by tooling: `sdd-check` fails a missing section (`SDD_NO_DIAGRAM_BLOCK`) or an empty one (`SDD_DIAGRAM_BLOCK_EMPTY`). Beyond the floor the author adds more views by judgment; that is not a gate.

Before writing any operator-facing artifact, recall the language rules — `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` (bureaucratic noun-for-verb phrasing, literal calque, bookish word) and `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` (a branch name, «как обсуждали», a session-plan label) — and hold the text about to be written to them. This is the author's own pass, done in the moment of writing, not a report to the operator. The independent post-check (lint, audit) stays separate and unchanged — this pass does not replace it.

A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.

SddInterface.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INTAKE` | Empty intake | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Spec exists + mode verb absent (per `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`) | | `H_BREAKING_CHANGE_NO_PROTOCOL` | A breaking interface change without a declared breaking-change protocol | | `H_PIVOT_NO_INVALIDATION_LIST` | `pivot` mode without a Pivot Invalidation List | | `H_REWRITE_WITH_DOWNSTREAM` | `rewrite` mode but the scope already has tickets — not v0, use `pivot` (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`) | | `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` | External-deps step finished without a Bootstrap Requirements section | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the spec |

Step.Action: State from the router gives the portal + scope-type (interface). Resolve the scope name; stat the spec → `greenfield` or detect the mode per `AX_DIRECTIVE_MODE` / `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`.

Step.Goal: Confirm interface and outline the section set.
Step.Action: Confirm scope-type, outline sections. Approval Check. STOP.

Per `AX_INTERFACE_FLOW`: schema format (OpenAPI / gRPC proto / JSON Schema / GraphQL), versioning scheme (semver / date-based / none), namespacing — Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses separated per `AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE`. Then run the operator interview — `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interview-protocol.directive.xml")` — passing scope-type `interface` (selects the TopicCatalog block) and the confirmed `scale:` from the session file: per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` `fix` / `function` → base topics + the triage minimum; `product` → the full scope-type block. The interview IS the substance of the step. Approval Check. STOP.

Versioning scheme + breaking-change protocol + consumer-notification rule — each locked choice recorded as a Decision Log entry (`AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`). A breaking change without a protocol → `H_BREAKING_CHANGE_NO_PROTOCOL`. STOP.
Backward-compat guarantees + consumer declaration (which scopes consume this contract, per `AX_CROSS_SCOPE_DEPENDENCIES`). STOP.

Walk the drafted spec; extract external assumptions; classify `exists` | `missing` | `unknown` (narrow read for inventory only, per `AX_BOOTSTRAP_NARROW_READ` and `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE` — design stays sourced from specs); resolve with the operator; materialize the Bootstrap Requirements table. Empty only if explicit «nothing to bootstrap», else `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING`.

In `greenfield`/`rewrite` mode, when `specs//.spec.md` does not exist yet, create its skeleton via `sdd-new interface --scope ` — it never overwrites and prints the section manifest (which sections are REQUIRED and what to fill); in `refine`/`pivot` mode the file already exists, edit it in place, skip `sdd-new`. Content guidance per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/interface-spec-structure.xml")`. Before writing, run the self-check pass per `AX_ARTIFACT_STYLE_SELF_CHECK`. In `refine` mode update sections in place per `AX_LIVING_SPEC`. In `pivot` mode also `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/pivot-formats.xml")` (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`); in `rewrite` mode write fresh — no supersession. For a brand-new scope, append the `🚧 (awaiting root sync)` placeholder row to the portal Scopes table per `AX_PORTAL_READ_ONLY_WITH_PLACEHOLDER_EXCEPTION` — every other portal edit belongs to the root flow. Write in review-state per `AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE` — prepend a `CHANGE_MANIFEST` (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/change-manifest.xml")`) and mark changed lines `✚`/`~` (greenfield → manifest only, no per-line marks); compress folds it to master downstream after the change ships. Then close with the integrity check per `AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK`: run `sdd-check --all specs/` (anchor balance + required sections + links) and resolve any finding. Then `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/review-lifecycle.directive.xml")` — internal critic → publish (MR) → external review → compress + merge on approval. After the spec merges to master, handoff is to scaffold (interface scopes have no modules). Approval Check. STOP.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words (no `Q` numbering, no semantic question IDs); under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name — never restore `Q` labels or per-question IDs; that bare-numbered shape without the tool is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### 💡 Формат хранения токенов Нужно решить, где держать design-токены: сгенерированный JSON проще парсить скриптам, а TS-модуль даёт автокомплит в IDE — для одного пакета без внешних потребителей разница небольшая. ✅ **JSON-файл** `[tokens.json]` — проще парсить любым языком, ничего специфичного для TS. Иначе: - **TS-модуль** `[tokens.ts]` — _за: автокомплит и типы · против: непортируемо за пределы TS_
(AskUserQuestion: «JSON-файл (рекомендую)» · «TS-модуль»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:
### 💡 Стратегия миграции v1→v2 Три пути дают разный профиль риска и времени простоя, и откат стоит по-разному в каждом. - **Big-bang** `[migrate-all]` — _за: один переход, нет промежуточного состояния · против: долгий простой, откат дорогой_ - **Постепенная миграция по скоупам** `[migrate-incremental]` — _за: откат дешёвый, риск размазан во времени · против: два формата сосуществуют дольше_ - **Parallel-run с shadow-чтением** `[migrate-shadow]` — нетипичный вариант, но снимает риск отката почти полностью ценой временной инфраструктуры
(AskUserQuestion: «Big-bang» · «Постепенная миграция» · «Parallel-run (нетипичный)»)
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative, still explained before the call:
### 💡 Нужен ли отдельный interface-скоуп Все текущие потребители — web; про API и будущих клиентов явно не говорили. ✅ **Пока не выделять** — можно добавить позже без миграции. _или сразу выделить, если API уже в планах?_
(AskUserQuestion: «Пока не выделять (рекомендую)» · «Выделить сразу»)

SddInterface.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `📐 CON_R · · · conf=`. Breadcrumb milestones (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Interface · Versioning · Compatibility · Spec.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch) `` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT` (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; add a diagram per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` if it is a flow ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_FORMAT` ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👨‍💻` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.
One line under the service line: this session's milestones, each rendered ` `, with a status marker chosen for legibility on BOTH light and dark themes — no half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓`) anywhere, they vanish depending on theme. Status set: `✅` done · `👨‍💻` active (the step running now) · `◻️` not yet reached. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`Vision ✅ · Scope Graph 👨‍💻 · Infra ◻️ · Portal ◻️`
The agent's compressed read of the task — its own confirmation of blind spots so the operator can catch a misread. A `### 🤔 Как я понял задачу` section near the TOP, then an italic blockquote, 2–3 sentences: the essence + the single riskiest assumption, with the assumption linked to the question that resolves it BY WORDING — there are no question numbers or IDs left to point at, so name the question itself. Never a restate of settled content.
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу > квинтэссенция — что считаю главным. > **Где могу ошибаться:** самое хрупкое допущение — это вопрос «<формулировка вопроса>».
A sub-topic dive inside a step collapses to two lines, not a five-field Return Summary:
→ ушли в `<тема>` ← `<итог одной фразой>`
When a decision is about a flow — data moving, state transitions, start / stop conditions — draw a tiny ASCII diagram; one glance beats a paragraph. This is the one place a fenced block is allowed inside an operator message (alignment matters). Keep it small.
``` [сеть] [auth] [конфиг] ──всё есть──► ОПРОС идёт ▲ │ └──── снова есть ──── ПАУЗА ◄───────┘ что-то пропало ```
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.

ArtifactOutput.Contract: ```markdown ### D-NNN — - **Status:** active | superseded | rejected | deferred - **Recorded:** session , - **Why:** <operator's own wording> - **Risk accepted:** - **Rejected alternatives:** - **Supersedes:** D-NNN (when superseding a prior decision) ```
